notes: Nigeria Hardening I Adoption Gate. Border-cash project claims only (NG-B1 / NG-B6 / NG-B7). Adopted from M2.5-reviewed candidates; vocabularies are not mechanical maps from supported/bounded. Does not draft data/rules/nigeria.json. Dual declaration operators are preserved. Numeric NGN traveller exception remains not established. Legacy FEMMPA s.12 US$5,000 is superseded temporal audit only.

claims.subject: Entry cash / negotiable-instrument declaration (statutory)
claims.rule: Transportation of cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent by individuals into Nigeria shall be declared to the Nigeria Customs Service
claims.scope: border entry; cash or negotiable instruments; individual travellers
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-001; reviewed fingerprint sha256:192062fcdd12413970f59aa55f510fb2e77dd2d882dadbffaabf86dde2d69323; MLPPA 2022 s.3(3) entry limb; statutory operator remains 'in excess of' (>), not >=
forbidden_inferences: declaration threshold is a carrying ceiling

claims.subject: Exit cash / negotiable-instrument declaration (statutory)
claims.rule: Transportation of cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent by individuals out of Nigeria shall be declared to the Nigeria Customs Service
claims.scope: border exit; cash or negotiable instruments; individual travellers
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-002; reviewed fingerprint sha256:6a23f5bb209722fd816938be92968dfa51a7ed47e65c1c57d19bb9c54b94ab52; MLPPA 2022 s.3(3) exit limb; statutory operator remains 'in excess of' (>); does not establish a general outbound carriage ceiling
forbidden_inferences: amount declared on entry as universal outbound ceiling
declaration threshold is a carrying ceiling

claims.subject: False or failed cash declaration offence consequence
claims.rule: Any person who falsely declares or fails to make a declaration to the Nigeria Customs Service under section 12 of the Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act commits an offence and is liable on conviction to forfeit the undeclared funds or negotiable instrument or to imprisonment for a term of at least two years or both
claims.scope: border entry or exit declaration failure / false declaration
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-003; reviewed fingerprint sha256:ab5cd17b7b4429656ce75a781b742940edfd83e6d8ae503504da779e4e252e66; uses M2.5 reviewed_text restoring statutory 'liable on conviction' (not softened 'may lead'); MLPPA 2022 s.3(4)-(5) pinpoint; Customs-to-CBN reporting chain not adopted
allowed_wording: imprisonment for a term of at least two years

claims.subject: Declaration rule is not itself a prohibition on genuine funds above threshold
claims.rule: The reviewed official CBN guidance states that the declaration rule for cash or negotiable instruments above US$10,000 does not itself prohibit genuinely owned or obtained funds above that amount from being brought into Nigeria or taken outside the country
claims.scope: border entry or exit; declaration vs prohibition distinction only
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-004; reviewed fingerprint sha256:2ce7ee95f4585498c81401675b5951278c6afb3fbe52c4f9e4c06099665df3d2; CBN 2013 clarification; narrow negative only — does not establish unrestricted carriage or absence of other Nigerian-law limits
forbidden_inferences: no ceiling exists under all Nigerian law
foreign currency can be taken without limit

claims.subject: Imported cash domiciliary-account withdrawal / re-export condition (FEMMPA s.21)
claims.rule: Where a person imports foreign currency in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent in cash and not by means of a bank draft, mail or telegraphic transfer and deposits the foreign currency in a domiciliary account with an authorised dealer, withdrawals from that account may be made only in cash, and that imported cash is exportable from Nigeria only in cash
claims.scope: imported cash deposited in a domiciliary account with an authorised dealer; cash-not-transfer condition retained
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-005; reviewed fingerprint sha256:bcb07b851173383e58f1b9506e2a5bff697bf4c9cf260009276a2c11582c34ba; FEMMPA 1995 s.21(1)-(2) with restored cash-not-transfer condition; not a universal outbound traveller rule
allowed_wording: not by means of a bank draft, mail or telegraphic transfer
exportable from Nigeria only in cash
forbidden_inferences: outbound foreign currency is limited to amount declared on entry
every departing traveller requires authorised-dealer documentation
s.21 establishes a universal outbound carriage ceiling

claims.subject: Customs e-CDF operational declaration trigger
claims.rule: Current Customs operational guidance on the e-currency declaration form uses a declaration trigger of US$10,000 or more / equal to or greater than US$10,000
claims.scope: Nigeria Customs Service e-CDF operational guidance; does not amend statutory MLPPA operator
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-006; reviewed fingerprint sha256:1f35bc49455e3c7d3fcfb1dd33691747b4fc36565474e06a59c43004cbd59715; operational operator >= only; Hardening I-B dual-operator preservation vs MLPPA > remains; Customs >= does not formally amend statutory >
allowed_wording: equal to or greater than US$10,000

claims.subject: Legacy FEMMPA s.12 US$5,000 statistical declaration threshold
claims.rule: FEMMPA 1995 section 12 states that foreign currency in excess of US$5,000 or its equivalent, whether being imported into or exported out of Nigeria, shall be declared on the prescribed form for reasons of statistics only. That older threshold wording is retained for temporal audit and must not drive the current border-cash declaration threshold while MLPPA 2022 section 3(3) uses in excess of US$10,000
claims.scope: temporal audit only; not a current traveller threshold
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-007; reviewed fingerprint sha256:12725ae59a82f23f97f1e9634f61792af23d42fcb1941c394a58bd67e318b864; historical/superseded role; must not enter current-rule field bindings
forbidden_inferences: travellers must declare above US$5,000 under current AML law

claims.subject: Physical naira import/export prohibition baseline
claims.rule: The importation and exportation of the naira remain prohibited except as permitted under guidelines issued from time to time by the Central Bank
claims.scope: cross-border physical naira notes; prohibition baseline only; current numeric traveller exception not established in this review
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-NGN-001; reviewed fingerprint sha256:165c2cb6d5132261f2a369c6a7a9b85479332030df92d9cca1bcb86334223647; FEMMPA 1995 s.14; Hardening I-B numeric exception not established — do not invent N10,000 / N20,000 / N100,000
allowed_wording: importation and exportation of the naira remain prohibited
current numeric traveller exception not established
forbidden_inferences: travellers may carry NGN up to a stated numeric limit
